claims.claim: Mock providers give deterministic, predictable responses
Mock providers work without an internet connection
promptarena run --mock-provider
--mock-provider is a flag of the run subcommand
--mock-provider replaces all configured providers with a generic mock
The mock provider simulates only the LLM decision; tools called by the mock still execute for real through the tool loop
--mock-config is a flag that takes a mock responses file
Top-level key scenarios maps scenario names to turn definitions
Scenario keys must match the scenario's metadata.name, not spec.id
Each scenario has a turns mapping keyed by turn number
A turn value may be a plain string meaning a text response
Top-level default_response field is used when no scenario or turn matches
A turn value mapping supports the keys response and tool_calls
promptarena run --mock-provider --mock-config mock-responses.yaml
apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 for Provider resources
kind Provider
spec.type mock selects the mock provider type
spec.model is a field on provider spec
spec.additional_config is a free-form map on provider spec
additional_config.mock_config points to a mock file, resolved relative to the arena config directory
tool_calls on a turn triggers real tool execution
Turn mapping key response holds the text of the turn
tool_calls entries have name and arguments fields
Example tool name check_subscription_status (illustrative, must be a tool the reader defines)
Turn numbers count each round of the tool loop: a tool-calling turn and the follow-up text turn are counted separately
A turn with tool_calls and no response is valid
A scenario's default_response covers turns with no explicit entry
Top-level default_response covers scenarios with no match at all
default_response is a valid field on a scenario entry in the mock file
config.arena.yaml spec.providers entries reference provider files via a file key
spec.scenarios entries reference scenario files via a file key
promptarena run --scenario customer-support
--override-provider from=to is a repeatable flag
--override-provider rewrites the from provider with the spec of the to provider
Overridden provider applies to candidate selection, self-play roles and judges
A judge that references a mock provider is used in the default run
--override-provider mock-judge=claude makes the judge run against claude
--override-provider claude=mock requires a defined provider named mock
Both from and to of --override-provider must be defined in spec.providers
Error text: unknown target provider "nonexistent" (must be defined in spec.providers)
promptarena run --mock-provider --mock-config dev-mocks.yaml
promptarena run --mock-provider --format junit
--format accepts the value junit
promptarena run --provider openai-gpt4
promptarena run --mock-provider --ci --format junit
The junit report is written to out/junit.xml
OPENAI_API_KEY is the env var read by the OpenAI provider
promptarena run --provider openai-gpt4 --ci
Top-level mock scenario key customer-support matches a scenario metadata.name
Tool name get_customer_info (illustrative, used in the example)
config.arena.yaml providers entries use the file key
--provider selects which provider a run uses
--override-provider swaps one provider for another at run time
examples/mock-config-example.yaml exists in the repository
examples/customer-support/ exists and compares mock vs real providers
A misspelled or snake_case mock file key such as default_response is an error when Arena loads the file
promptarena validate checks the mock_config file of each type: mock provider; promptarena run also checks the --mock-config file
The mock file check also rejects unknown keys inside a turn, a tool call and a content part
